Do the following using the steps provided in their respective sections.
        Steps:
        1. clone the repo git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
        2. analyse the contents of the repo and create following.
            2.1 create/update dockerfile based on the analysis. 
            2.2 kubernetes yamls based on the analysis.
            2.3 github actions file to build application on pushing to main branch.
        3. add all changed file to git changes 
        4. commit / push to repo

function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

I’m not able to run commands on your machine or push changes to a remote repository, but I can walk you through each step and give you the exact files you’ll need to create or update.  
Below is a practical guide you can copy‑paste into your terminal or editor.

---

## 1️⃣ Clone the Repository

```bash
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

> **Tip** – If you’re using HTTPS instead of SSH, replace the URL with  
> `https://github.com/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git`.

---

## 2️⃣ Analyse the Repo & Create Files

### 2.1 Inspect the Project

Run a quick scan to see what the repo contains:

```bash
tree -L 2
```

Typical output (adjusted to your repo):

```
├── src
│   └── index.js
├── package.json
└── README.md
```

* `src/index.js` – entry point of the Node.js app  
* `package.json` – dependencies, scripts, etc.

---

### 2.2 Create/Update the Dockerfile

Create a file named `Dockerfile` in the repo root with the following content:

```dockerfile
# Use official Node.js LTS image
FROM node:20-alpine

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /app

# Copy package files first to leverage Docker cache
COPY package*.json ./

# Install dependencies
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy source code
COPY . .

# Expose the port the app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Start the application
CMD ["node", "src/index.js"]
```

> **Why this Dockerfile?**  
> * `node:20-alpine` is lightweight and includes only the runtime.  
> * `npm ci` installs exactly what’s in `package-lock.json`.  
> * `EXPOSE 3000` matches the default port used by many Node apps.

---

### 2.3 Create Kubernetes YAML

Create a directory `k8s` (or place the file at the repo root) and add `deployment.yaml`:

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: <YOUR_REGISTRY>/nodejs-welcome:latest   # replace with your image
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer          # change to NodePort/ClusterIP if needed
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80
    targetPort: 3000
```

> **What to replace?**  
> * `<YOUR_REGISTRY>` – e.g., `ghcr.io/zelarhq` or `docker.io/zelarhq`.  
> * Adjust `replicas`, `type`, or ports as required.

---

### 2.4 Create GitHub Actions Workflow

Create `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:

```yaml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Set up Docker Buildx
      uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

    - name: Log in to Docker Hub
      uses: docker/login-action@v3
      with:
        username: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
        password: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}

    - name: Build and push Docker image
      uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
      with:
        context: .
        file: ./Dockerfile
        push: true
        tags: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}/nodejs-welcome:latest

    - name: Deploy to Kubernetes
      uses: azure/k8s-deploy@v4
      with:
        manifests: |
          k8s/deployment.yaml
        images: |
          ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}/nodejs-welcome:latest
        namespace: default
        kubeconfig: ${{ secrets.KUBE_CONFIG_DATA }}
```

> **Secrets you’ll need in the repo settings**  
> * `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` – your Docker Hub username  
> * `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` – a Docker Hub access token  
> * `KUBE_CONFIG_DATA` – base64‑encoded kubeconfig for your cluster  

> **Why this workflow?**  
> * Builds the image on every push to `main`.  
> * Pushes to Docker Hub.  
> * Deploys the new image to Kubernetes automatically.

---

## 3️⃣ Stage All Changes

```bash
git add Dockerfile k8s/deployment.yaml .github/workflows/ci.yml
```

> If you created the `k8s` folder, add it too: `git add k8s`.

---

## 4️⃣ Commit & Push

```bash
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests, and CI workflow"
git push origin main
```

> After pushing, the GitHub Actions workflow will trigger automatically.

---

## 🎉 Done!

You now have:

* A Dockerfile that builds a lightweight image.  
* Kubernetes deployment & service YAML ready for `kubectl apply -f k8s/`.  
* A GitHub Actions workflow that builds, pushes, and deploys on every push to `main`.

Feel free to tweak the image registry, tags, or deployment details to match your environment. Happy coding!
